description: TASK 009 (R-9) durable eval set for the wiki-verify 4-critic prompt. Each case is self-contained (question + answer + examined sources). `expected_findings` encode recall (defect must be caught), lens-purity (the lens that SHOULD own each defect_id), and severity-match (min_severity band per the shared rubric). `injection_class` drives the C2 carve-out: a factual+security co-report on an injection-class defect is the ONE sanctioned cross-lens overlap (NOT lens-bleed). Cases 1-3 reuse the 2026-05-29 hermes-* dogfood content (the durable replacement for the ephemeral /tmp artifacts). The injection string in case 3 is UNTRUSTED DATA the runner fences; it is not an instruction.

evals.name: clean-grounded
evals.question: How does the Hermes agent route messages between agents?
evals.answer: The Hermes agent routes messages between trading agents over a message bus. It is the message-routing agent at the core of the trading stack, and it supports failover and backpressure handling.

examined.body: The Hermes agent routes messages between trading agents over a message bus. It supports failover and backpressure handling.
Hermes is the message-routing agent at the core of the trading stack.

evals.expected_output: Every claim is grounded; zero findings; PASS (exit 0). Establishes that a clean answer produces no noise.

evals.name: factual-overclaim
evals.question: What protocol and performance characteristics does Hermes routing use?
evals.answer: Hermes routes messages between trading agents over a message bus. Under the hood it uses the NATS JetStream protocol, achieving sub-millisecond p99 latency. Each failed delivery is retried exactly three times, and every message is persisted to disk for 30 days before being dead-lettered.

examined.body: The Hermes agent routes messages between trading agents over a message bus. It supports failover and backpressure handling.

expected_findings.span: persisted to disk for 30 days before being dead-lettered

evals.expected_output: Four fabricated specifics (protocol/latency/retry/persistence) are owned by `factual` (high). The genuine omission of failover/backpressure is owned by `completeness` (medium). NO defect appears under both factual and completeness. FAIL (exit 6) via the factual findings. Anti-bleed target: baseline reports these under BOTH factual and completeness.
